I'm 70 this year. I've been farming these same 6 mu and a bit for 50 years — since I was a young man of 20. Never went to school, can't read much, but I know this land better than anyone. It's just me and the old woman now. Our son works in Shijiazhuang, sends a bit of money when he can, but not much. We're on a tight budget. Every yuan I spend on the field is one less for medicine or food, so I don't throw money around like some of the younger farmers.

I split the land like I always have: about 5 mu for wheat-maize, which is our main food and income, and the remaining 1.8 mu on the south side for cotton. The old woman still wants the cotton — we've grown it forever, and she knows how to pick it. At our age, cotton is hard on the back, but we manage.

**Wheat** — I planted last October, around the 10th, same time as always. I used improved seed, about 30 jin per mu, cost me around 30 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that's roughly 25 kg per mu. Then in spring, when the wheat starts turning green, I'll topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. I don't use as much as young Zhang down the road — he puts on a lot more, but he's younger and has more money. Last year I used about this much and got around 750 jin per mu, which is fine for us. I'll irrigate three times: once right after planting (already done), once at jointing in April, and once when the grain is filling in May. Water from the well costs money — about 40 yuan each time — but you can't skip it for wheat. I hire the combine for harvest, about 70 yuan per mu. Me and the old woman handle the rest. I expect about 380 kg per mu this year if the weather holds.

**Maize** — Goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 12th. Very tight window — sometimes only 3 or 4 days between cutting wheat and putting in maize. I hire a tractor with a planter if I can get it, about 35 yuan per mu. Hybrid seed is expensive, about 45 yuan per mu, but you need it these days. I put compound fertilizer in at planting, about 20 kg per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 15 kg per mu. Irrigate twice if it doesn't rain — once at jointing, once at filling. Should get about 420 kg per mu.

**Cotton** — On the 1.8 mu, I plant around April 22nd. I save most of my own seed, just buy a little to refresh, so seed cost is low, maybe 15 yuan per mu. One application of compound fertilizer at planting, about 20 kg per mu, and a handful of urea — about 10 kg — when it flowers. Irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are setting. Cotton needs picking by hand. Me and the old woman pick it ourselves over September and October, three or four times. I expect about 200 kg of lint per mu, maybe a bit less if the bolls don't open well.

I don't hire much labor except for the combine and sometimes for maize planting when the window is tight. Labor costs 100 yuan per day now, too expensive for us. Total costs me about 4,800 yuan for all inputs. It's a lot when you're living on a small pension and a few mu of land. But if I don't spend it, I don't eat.
